mix_frequency_estimate: CALL ~75% / FOLD ~25% (pure-strategy lean to CALL with NFD+A-blocker; FOLD branch reserved for villain ranges skewed toward sets/two-pair that crush implied odds)
reasoning: Spot identification: turn decision OOP in BB on Jc7s5d2h (2h blanks the rainbow flop) with AsKs (nut flush draw + AK overcards), facing a turn raise in a chain BET_RAISE sequence. Preflop was CO 2.5bb open, BTN flat, BB flat — three-way SRP, BB OOP-early to both villains. Per-villain range chains: the turn raiser's range in a BET_RAISE spot through TWO opponents is heavily condensed — top-pair+ with kicker concerns wanting protection (KJ/AJ/QJ/JT), two-pair (J7s/J5s/75s rare), sets (JJ/77/55 — turn raises with these are GTO-standard for protection), and a sliver of polar bluffs (combo draws like 86s/64s/A4s with backdoor). The original bettor between hero and raiser is now squeezed and folds out most non-pair-plus holdings, so the raise is also a leverage-bet against the bettor's c-bet-and-give-up frequency, not purely a value-shove vs hero. Equity/range tensions: AsKs has ~19.6% raw to make the nut flush by river (9 outs, one card to come if only turn → roughly 19%; though with the river also live in standard line: ~35% to hit flush by river, but hero only sees one card before next decision). Critical: A-blocker removes AA, AJ, A5s, A7s combos from raiser's value AND removes A-high combo-draw bluffs (AhXh, A4s-A2s with spade backdoors are reduced). The K-blocker removes KJ value combos. Realized equity multiway is degraded but hero is now effectively HU vs the raiser (original bettor will fold), so realization ≈ 0.9 — close to clean. Pot odds: 18 to call into 28+18 = 46 pot → need 39% direct equity OR direct + implied. Direct flush equity to river is ~35-36%, just short of 39%. Implied odds on the As when flush completes are large: villain's sets and two-pair stack off on spade rivers, easily covering the 4% gap. Two overcard outs (A/K to top pair) are partially dirty against villain's set-heavy range, so I discount them to ~3-4% effective. Decision: CALL. Bucket: turn-combo-draw-facing-raise-with-overcards-and-blocker. CALL realizes the nut-draw equity with sufficient implied odds and blocker-reduced value density on the raiser's side. RAISE (semi-bluff) is dominated because villain's range after a multi-way turn raise is too condensed to fold meaningful value, and shoving 100bb-ish stacks turns AsKs into a pure-bluff with only 35% equity. FOLD is the closest alternative — defensible if villain's raise is read as set-only — but giving up a nut-draw with blocker effects against any realistically balanced raise range is too tight and bleeds EV across the population.
